(He is forbidden) because in what has been revealed to you there is what spares you from asking.
(وَلا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فاعِلٌ ذلِكَ غَداً إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تقولن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa because it is joined to the nūn of emphasis, in the position of a jussive by لا; the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "anta"; لشيء is attached to تقولن, i.e. for the sake of something you undertake and are concerned with; it is also said that the lām means في — this has been mentioned before. The hamza of إن is given kasra because it is preceded by the verb of saying. Inna and its noun are the maqūl al-qawl; فاعل is the khabar of inna; ذلك is the object of فاعل; غدا is an adverb attached to فاعل. إلا أن يشاء الله is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the most general of states, i.e. do not say of anything in any state except in the state of your being bound up with the will (of Allah) and making it conditional on it; so أن with what follows is a ḥāl, and the implied form is "do not say 'I will do it tomorrow' except saying 'if Allah wills'". It is also said that the implied form is "except with (bi-) Allah's willing", so the maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition with its genitive is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "except bound up with saying 'if Allah wills'". It is also said that the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) and that the position of أن يشاء الله is accusative as an excepted noun.
Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī excelled in the i'rab of this verse; his text is: "Concerning what is excepted from, there are three views. The first: it is from the prohibition, and the meaning is 'do not say "I will do (it) tomorrow" unless you are given permission to say it'. The second: it is from the fāʿil of تقولن, i.e. do not say 'I will be doing (it) tomorrow' until you join to it the saying 'if Allah wills'. The third: it is disconnected. The position of أن يشاء الله is accusative on two views. The first is as an excepted noun, the implied form being 'do not say that at any time except at the time that Allah wills', i.e. permits; the time is omitted though intended. The second is that it is a ḥāl, the implied form being 'do not say "I will do (it) tomorrow" except saying "if Allah wills"'; the saying is omitted — and this is frequent — and His words أن يشاء are given the meaning of إن شاء, which is a case of construing according to the meaning. It is also said that the implied form is 'except with Allah's willing', i.e. bound up with saying 'if Allah wills'."
In sum, the purpose of forbidding this saying is (to forbid) its not being joined with the mention of (Allah's) will. This is a prohibition of instruction in manners, (revealed) when the Jews said to Quraysh: "Ask Muhammad about the spirit, the Companions of the Cave and Dhū al-Qarnayn." They asked him, and he said: "Come to me tomorrow and I will tell you" — and he did not make the exception (saying "if Allah wills"). So the revelation was delayed for him until it weighed on him, and Quraysh called him a liar. Mention of the interruption of revelation will come in the Benefits section.
(وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ إِذا نَسِيتَ وَقُلْ عَسى أَنْ يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّي لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هذا رَشَداً): واذكر is conjoined to what precedes; ربك is the mafʿūl bihi, and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "the will of your Lord". إذا is an adverb attached to اذكر, i.e. when forgetfulness overtakes you; the clause نسيت is in the position of a genitive as the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb; its answer is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then remember". وقل is conjoined to اذكر. عسى is one of the verbs of hope; its noun is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; أن يهديني — أن with what is in its domain — is the khabar; ربي is the fāʿil of يهديني; لأقرب is attached to يهديني; من هذا is attached to أقرب; رشدا is a tamyīz (specification), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "that He guide me with a guidance", so that it agrees in meaning with its governing verb. The first is more likely, i.e. to something nearer in guiding people and indicating that. The demonstrative هذا points to what preceded of the account of the Companions of the Cave and their wondrous story, which has now concluded.
(وَلَبِثُوا فِي كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلاثَ مِائَةٍ سِنِينَ وَازْدَادُوا تِسْعاً): ولبثوا is conjoined to what precedes, to settle the dispute and remove the doubt arising from the disagreement about them and the length of their stay. في كهفهم is attached to لبثوا; ثلاث is an adverb and مائة the muḍāf ilayhi; سنين is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) for ثلاثمائة, or a badal (substitute). It cannot be a tamyīz, because the tamyīz of مائة is genitive, its genitive being by annexation, and the tanwīn prevents annexation. The discussion of number will come in detail in the Benefits section. ازدادوا is a verb and its fāʿil; تسعا is the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. nine years.
(قُلِ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما لَبِثُوا): الله is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم a khabar, and the clause is the maqūl al-qawl; بما is attached to أعلم; the clause لبثوا is the ṣila of the relative, i.e. the time during which they stayed.
(لَهُ غَيْبُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ): له is a preposed khabar and غيب السموات والأرض a postponed mubtadaʾ. أبصر is a form of wonder (taʿajjub); it is a past verb that has come in the form of the imperative, its meaning being declarative; the bāʾ is added to the fāʿil to improve the wording. The discussion of the two forms of wonder will come in the Rhetoric section [Translator's note: in fact it comes in the Benefits section]. أسمع is conjoined to أبصر.
(ما لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا يُشْرِكُ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَداً): ما is negative; لهم is a preposed khabar; من دونه is a ḥāl; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ولي is a postponed mubtadaʾ in position. ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; يشرك is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil; في حكمه is attached to يشرك; أحدا is the mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
The discussion of these verses and the rhetorical devices they contain would be very long; we shall incline to brevity as far as possible, and say:
1- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «يتنازعون بينهم أمرهم» there is an implicit metaphor: He likened their affair to a thing over which there is much pulling and contention, then omitted that thing and borrowed the contention around it.
And in the saying of Allah the Exalted «رجما بالغيب» there is also an implicit metaphor: He likened the unseen and hidden to a thing that is pelted with stones, and borrowed pelting (rajm) for it.
2- The wāw of eight (wāw al-thamāniya) and the dispute raging around it:
We promised you to bring the views about the wāw entering ثامنهم in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم», and we have presented in the I'rab the view we chose among them. A number of great men of letters said that it is the wāw of eight. Ibn Hishām said: "The wāw of eight has been mentioned by a group of men of letters such as al-Ḥarīrī, of weak grammarians such as Ibn Khālawayh, and of exegetes such as al-Thaʿlabī. They claimed that when the Arabs count they say 'six, seven, and eight', to signal that seven is a complete number and that what comes after it is a new number. They adduced as evidence for this several verses, one of them «سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم» up to His saying, glory be to Him, «وثامنهم كلبهم». It is said that it is there for conjoining one clause to another, since the implied form is 'they are seven'; then it is said that the whole is their speech, and it is said that the conjunction is the speech of Allah the Exalted, the meaning being 'Yes, they are seven, and their eighth is their dog', and that this is a confirmation of this statement just as رجما بالغيب is a refutation of that statement." After a long discussion he said: "I say: if the wāw of eight had any reality, the verse (of the gates of Paradise) would not be an instance of it, since there is no mention of a number in it at all; it only mentions 'the gates', which is a plural indicating no particular number. Moreover, the wāw does not enter upon it (the word 'eight'), but upon a clause in which it is."
Others said in rebuttal of those who claimed the existence of the wāw of eight — namely that there is in the language a wāw that accompanies the eighth and is specific to it: where is the mention of number in the gates of Paradise, such that it reaches the eighth and the wāw accompanies it? They sometimes count among its instances «والناهون عن المنكر», which is the eighth (attribute) from His saying «التائبون». This too is rejected, because the wāw is joined to this attribute only to link it with the one before it, namely «الآمرون بالمعروف», because of the affinity and connection between them. Do you not see their being joined in all the places where they come, as in His saying «يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر» and His saying «وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر»? Some have even counted among its instances the wāw in «ثيبات وأبكارا», because they found it with the eighth (attribute); this is a gross error, for this is the wāw of division (wāw al-taqsīm), and if you went and deleted it and said "thayyibātin abkāran", the speech would not stand [Translator's note: printed «لم يستدل», evidently for «لم يستقم»]. So it has become clear that what is meant in all these enumerated places comes for something other than what these people claimed [Translator's note: printed «ورادة» for «واردة»].
I say: if the wāw were dropped from أبكار, the meaning would be disturbed, because they cannot be previously-married and virgins at the same time; so the wāw was necessary to indicate difference. Al-Qāḍī al-Fāḍil, the master of the artful style in prose composition, used to believe that the wāw in this verse is redundant and boasted of having discovered it, saying it is the wāw of eight — until he mentioned that in the presence of the Shaykh Abū al-Jūd al-Muqriʾ [Translator's note: printed «أبو الجود» where the genitive «أبي الجود» is expected], who showed him that he was mistaken [Translator's note: printed «وأهم» for «واهم»] and that necessity calls for its entry, otherwise the meaning would be corrupted, unlike the wāw of eight, which is brought for no need. He said: "You have guided us aright, O Abū al-Jūd."
Among those who supported the existence of the wāw of eight is the Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī. And the learned al-Kāfiyajī made a charming and fair statement on this subject, which we cite in its exact words:
"In reality it is the wāw of conjunction; but since its use is specific to a particular place, and it contains a strange matter and a subtle consideration, it was fitting that it be called by a name other than that of its kind. So it was called the wāw of eight because of an affinity between it and seven. This is because seven, for them, is a complete unit like the units of the tens, since it comprises most of the ranks of the basic numbers, so that eight is a new unit; hence there is a connection between them in one respect and a separation in another, and this is what calls for the conjunction. This meaning does not exist between seven and six.
"I say: the explanation of the completeness of seven is that a number is either single (odd), or composed of two singles, which is the pair (even), or of a pair and a single, or of two pairs. The first of these three (composite types) is three, which includes one and two, and the last is four. The sum of three and four is seven, so with it the basic (types) are complete, and what comes after is repetition: eight is a pair and a pair, which has already passed, nine is a pair and a single, and so on."
More of this discussion will come in speaking about «وفتحت أبوابها» and «ثيبات وأبكارا», for the discussion has grown very long.

* Benefits:
1- The rules of number and its tamyīz (specification):
The specifier of a number is of two kinds, accusative and genitive. The genitive is of two kinds, singular and plural: the singular is the specifier of a hundred and a thousand, and the plural is the specifier of three to ten. The accusative is the specifier of eleven to ninety-nine, and it is only singular. Among what deviates from this is their saying "three hundred" (thalāthu miʾatin) up to "nine hundred", where they made do with the singular form instead of the plural. The one who said the following returned to the regular pattern:
ثلاث مئين للملوك وفي بها ... ردائي وجلت عن وجوه الاهاتم
(Three hundreds (of camels) for the kings — my cloak fulfilled them, and lifted (disgrace) from the faces of the Ahātim.) [Translator's note: printed «الاهاتم», i.e. «الأهاتم».]
He brought the specifier of "three" as a plural of the word "hundred", as regular analogy requires, even though it is anomalous in usage. In the specifier there are then two permissible options: following (the number) as a badal (substitute), e.g. ثلاثة أثواب, and the accusative as a tamyīz, e.g. ثلاثة أثوابا. And the saying of Allah the Exalted ثلاثمائة سنين is accusative as a badal or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) for ثلاثمائة.
This is the view of Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj. He said: it cannot be a tamyīz, because if it were a tamyīz, the least they stayed would have to be nine hundred years, since the explanatory (tamyīz) applies to each one of the number, and each one would be "years", which is plural, and the least a plural can be is three; so they would have stayed nine hundred years. Al-Farrāʾ allowed سنين to be a tamyīz, on the pattern of the poet's words:
فيها اثنتان وأربعون حلوبة ... سودا كخافية الغراب الأعصم
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the hidden wing-feathers of the aʿṣam raven.)
He said: that is because سودا, which is a plural, came in the tamyīz, since the naʿt (adjective) and the thing described are one thing. But the first view (is correct), because in second elements things are allowed that are not allowed in first elements; do you not see that you say "O Zayd the tall" (yā Zaydu al-ṭawīl), whereas if you said "O the tall" (yā al-ṭawīl) it would not be allowed?
This verse is by ʿAntara, from his Muʿallaqa, which begins:
هل غادر الشعراء من متردّم ... أم هل عرفت الدار بعد توهم
(Have the poets left any place in need of patching? Or did you recognise the abode after long reflection?)
And before the verse cited is:
ما راعني إلا حمولة أهلها ... وسط الديار تسف حب الخمخم
(Nothing alarmed me but the baggage camels of her people, in the midst of the abodes, munching the seeds of the khimkhim.)
Rāʿanī: it alarmed me. Al-ḥamūla: the camels on which loads are carried. Wasṭ is its adverb [Translator's note: so in the source, «ظرفه»]; when it is not an adverb the sīn is vowelled, and you say "the middle (wasaṭ) of the house is spacious". Tasiffu: they eat; one says safaftu al-dawāʾa asiffuhu (I swallowed the powdered medicine). Al-ḥalūba is the milked (she-camel); it is used for the singular and the plural in the same form. Al-khawāfī are the last feathers of the wing, next to the back. Al-asḥam is black [Translator's note: the verse as quoted above has «الأعصم»]. اثنتان is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أربعون is conjoined to it. His saying سودا is a naʿt of حلوبة, because it has a plural meaning, the meaning being "of the milch camels". The kāf in كخافية is in the position of an accusative, the meaning being "black like the hidden feathers of the black (asḥam) raven". From what we mentioned in explaining al-ḥalūba and its suitability to be applied to the singular and the plural, you will know what to make of their saying that the evidence in this verse is the permissibility of describing a singular specifier with a plural, and their claim that حلوبة is a singular specifier of the number described by a plural, namely سود, which is the plural of sawdāʾ. Al-Aʿlam claimed that his saying سودا is not a naʿt but a ḥāl (circumstantial) from اثنتان وأربعون; he said: "It is a ḥāl from an indefinite noun, and it could be nominative as a naʿt; it cannot be a naʿt of حلوبة, because it is singular when it is the tamyīz of a number, while سودا is plural, and the singular is not described by the plural." This is worth nothing, because they overlooked the secret, which is the application of حلوبة to both singular and plural.
We now summarise the rules of number in general:
The number words from three to nine are the opposite of the thing counted in masculine and feminine, whether they are single, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted «سخرها عليهم سبع ليال وثمانية أيام حسوما», or compound, as in "fifteen pens" (khamsata ʿashara qalaman) and "sixteen sheets" (sitta ʿashrata waraqatan), or conjoined, as in "twenty-three days" (thalāthatun wa-ʿishrūna yawman) and "twenty-four hours" (arbaʿun wa-ʿishrūna sāʿatan). As for one and two, they agree with the thing counted in all three cases. As for hundred and thousand, their form does not change for masculine and feminine; likewise the words for the tens, such as twenty and thirty — except ten, which is the opposite of the thing counted when it is single and agrees with it when it is compound.
From the number noun an adjective is formed on the pattern fāʿil, agreeing with the thing it describes. As for making a number definite: in the construct (number), al- enters on the muḍāf ilayhi; in the compound, al- enters on its first part; in the conjoined, al- enters on both parts.
As for the declension of numbers, it takes three forms:
1- With vowels, from one to ten, provided these are single and not compound — excepted from this are ithnān (two, masculine) and ithnatān (two, feminine), which are two words attached to the dual — and likewise the two numbers hundred and thousand.
2- With letters: this is the number ithnān for the masculine and ithnatān for the feminine, and the tens.
3- Indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa: these are the compound numbers, i.e. from eleven to nineteen and from "eleventh" to "nineteenth", except the first part of ithnā ʿashar (twelve), because it is attached to the dual, as has preceded.

The active participle derived from a number:
The active participle derived from a number is used in two senses:
The first: that what is meant by it is one of a group.
The second: that it is an agent like other active participles.
The first is like thānī ithnayn (the second of two) and thālith thalātha (the third of three). Allah the Exalted said: «لقد كفر الذين قالوا: إن الله ثالث ثلاثة», and He, Mighty and Majestic, said: «إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين». What is of this type is in pure (true) annexation, because its meaning is "one of three" and "part of three"; just as annexation of this is valid, so is that of what has its meaning. In the view of most grammarians it may not be given tanwīn and put the following noun in the accusative, because it is not taken from a governing verb. As for the second, which is an agent like other active participles, such as thālith ithnayn (the one who makes two into three), rābiʿ thalātha and khāmis arbaʿa: this is different from the first sense; its meaning is "the one who made the two three by himself", so its meaning is verbal, as if he said "the one who made them three (thallathahum), four (rabbaʿahum), five (khammasahum)". On this basis is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم», and likewise: «سيقولون ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم.... رجما بالغيب» and «ويقولون سبعة وثامنهم كلبهم». In this sense it may be given tanwīn and put what follows in the accusative, so you say: hādhā thālithun ithnayni wa-rābiʿun thalāthatan, because it is taken from thallathahum and rabbaʿahum, so it is like "this one is striking Zayd" (hādhā ḍāribun Zaydan); but the first is more frequent. Sībawayh said: "The Arabs seldom intend this", meaning khāmis arbaʿa (in the verbal sense). If you put it in construct, it is like ḍāribu Zaydin, so the annexation is not pure. This is when the present or future is intended; if the past is intended, only the dropping of the tanwīn and annexation are allowed, as is the case in your saying "this one struck Zayd yesterday" (hādhā ḍāribu Zaydin amsi).
2- Wonder (taʿajjub) and its forms in Arabic:
Wonder is an emotion that arises in the soul on perceiving a matter whose cause is hidden; hence it is said: "When the cause appears, wonder vanishes." It is not said of Allah that He wonders, since nothing is hidden from Him; and what occurs in the Qur'an that apparently suggests this is understood as directed to the addressee, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted «فما أصبرهم على النار», i.e. their state on that day is such that you, the addressee, ought to wonder at it. It is also said that wonder is regarding as great the act of an agent whose distinction in it is evident. Regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted here «أبصر به وأسمع», scholars have taken three positions:
1- That it is in the form of the imperative with a declarative meaning, and the bāʾ is added to the fāʿil to improve the wording. If you ask: how can the hāʾ be a fāʿil when it is an accusative or genitive pronoun? I say: it is only a convention, and that became admissible because of the overt presence of the bāʾ before it, and because the bāʾ was only added so that it would take the form of an object.
2- That the fāʿil is the pronoun of the maṣdar.
3- That the fāʿil is the pronoun of the addressee. Those who held this argued that the use of the imperative for the past is unknown. It is kept invariably singular and masculine, not put in the dual or plural or feminine, only because it is speech that has become like a proverb. This is one of the regular (qiyāsī) forms of wonder.
The second is mā afʿalahu ("how … he is!"). These two forms are the ones given chapters in the books of grammar, and they are the two regular ones. The meaning of ما, as Sībawayh said, is that it is a complete indefinite noun meaning "something", and it is put at the beginning (as mubtadaʾ) because it contains the meaning of wonder; the verbal clause after it is in the position of a nominative as its khabar (predicate). This is the correct view, because the intent of the one who wonders is to inform that the object of wonder has a distinction whose perception is clear while the reason for its being singled out by it is hidden; so the clause expressing that deserved to be opened with an unspecified indefinite noun, so that vagueness followed by clarification would be achieved.
There are other forms of wonder found in the Book, the ḥadīth and the speech of the Arabs. From the Book: «كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم»; from the ḥadīth, his ﷺ saying to Abū Hurayra: "Glory be to Allah! The believer does not become impure"; and from the speech of the Arabs: "To Allah be his merit as a horseman!" (lillāhi darruhu fārisan). But the grammarians did not give chapters to these forms, because they do not indicate wonder by their original coinage but by context.
Important issues:
1- One only expresses wonder at a definite noun or a specified indefinite noun; so one does not say "How happy a man is!" (mā asʿada rajulan), because there is no benefit in it.
2- The object of wonder may be omitted if it is a pronoun, as in the saying of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, as it is claimed:
جزى الله عني والجزاء بفضله ... ربيعة خيرا ما أعف وأكرما
(May Allah reward Rabīʿa well on my behalf — and reward is by His grace — how chaste and how generous (they are)!)
i.e. how chaste they are and how generous they are. We only said "as it is claimed" because this verse is not established as ʿAlī's. In al-Qāmūs, under the root «ودق», quoting al-Māzinī — and al-Zamakhsharī held it correct — it is not authentic that he uttered any poetry except two verses, namely his saying:
تلكم قريش تمناني لتقتلني ... فلا وربك لا برّوا ولا ظفروا
وإن هلكت فرهن ذمتي لهم ... بذات ودقين لا يعفو لها أثر
(There are Quraysh, wishing to meet me so as to kill me; no, by your Lord, they will neither be true nor victorious. And if I perish, my pledge is held for them in a calamity of two downpours whose trace will never be effaced.)
And in the pattern afʿil bihi (it may be omitted) if it is conjoined to another one mentioned with it, as in the verse «أبصر به وأسمع». It is omitted, although it is a fāʿil, only because its constant genitive gave it the appearance of an extra element (faḍla). Its omission without being conjoined to one like it is anomalous, as in the saying of ʿUrwa ibn al-Ward:
فذلك إن يلق المنية يلقها ... حميدا وإن يستغن يوما فأجدر
(That one, if he meets death, meets it praiseworthy; and if one day he becomes rich, how worthy (he is of it)!)
He omitted the object of wonder although it was not conjoined to one like it.
These two verbs are formed only from what fulfils eight conditions:
1- That it be a verb. Their saying mā adhraʿa al-marʾa ("how skilful the woman is!") is anomalous; they formed it from their saying imraʾa dhirāʿ, and al-dhirāʿ, on the pattern saḥāb, is a woman with light (nimble) hands in spinning. But Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ related in al-Afʿāl: dharuʿat al-marʾa, her hand was nimble in work, so she is dhirāʿ; on this basis there is no anomaly in their saying mā adhraʿa al-marʾa. Of the same kind is their saying mā ajdarahu bi-kadhā and mā aqmanahu bi-kadhā: the first they formed from their saying huwa qamīn bi-kadhā, and the second from huwa jadīr bi-kadhā [Translator's note: so in the source; the order is reversed — ajdar is from jadīr and aqman from qamīn]; the meaning of both is "how deserving he is of such", and they have no verb. But he said in al-Qāmūs: "jadura, like karuma, jadāratan; and it is a majdara that he should do (so), and majdūr, i.e. fitting; and jaddarahu: he made him worthy" — and so the grammarians' statement collapses from its foundation.
2- That the verb be triliteral; so they are not formed from a bare or augmented quadriliteral verb, nor from a triliteral augmented by one, two or three letters — except the pattern afʿala: it is said that they may be formed from it, whether its hamza is for transitivity or not, e.g. mā aẓlama al-layl ("how dark the night is!") and mā afqara hādhā al-makān ("how desolate this place is!"); and it is said that it is anomalous, what has been heard of it being preserved, as has preceded, and not taken as a basis for analogy. They said: mā aʿṭāhu li-al-dirham ("how generous he is with the dirham!"), mā awlāhu li-al-maʿrūf ("how ready he is to do kindness!") and mā attaqāhu Allāha ("how God-fearing he is!"). Likewise mā akhṣarahu ("how concise it is!") is anomalous, because it is from ikhtaṣara.
3- That the verb be inflectable (mutaṣarrif), because inflecting what is not inflected violates its original coinage; mā aʿsāhu and aʿsi bihi are anomalous.
4- That its meaning admit of degrees of excellence or difference; so they are not formed from such verbs as faniya (to perish), māta (to die) and ghariqa (to drown), because in them some agents have no distinction over others such that one would wonder at it.
5- That it be in the active voice; so they are not formed from the passive. Some excepted verbs that are always passive, such as ʿunītu bi-ḥājatika ("I was concerned with your need") and zuhiya ʿalaynā ("he was haughty towards us"), allowing wonder (from them) because there is no ambiguity; so you say mā aʿnāhu bi-ḥājatika and mā azhāhu ʿalaynā.
6- That it be complete (tāmm); so they are not formed from such verbs as kāna, kāda and ṣāra, because they are incomplete (nawāqiṣ). Ibn al-Sarrāj and al-Zajjāj reported: mā akwana Zaydan qāʾiman.
7- That it be affirmative; so they are not formed from a negated verb, whether it is always negated, such as mā ʿāja bi-al-dawāʾ ("he did not benefit from the medicine"), whose imperfect yaʿīju is also always negated — so the grammarians said, but their statement collapses because it has come non-negated: Abū ʿAlī al-Qālī related in his Nawādir: Thaʿlab recited to us from Ibn al-Aʿrābī:
ولم أر شيئا بعد ليلى ألذه ... ولا مشربا أروى به فأعيج
(After Laylā I have found nothing I relish, nor a drink by which I quench my thirst and so benefit.)
i.e. "and benefit from it" — or not always negated; (the reason is) so that the negative is not confused with the affirmative.
8- That its active participle not be on the pattern afʿal (feminine faʿlāʾ). So they are not formed from such verbs as ʿarija, giving aʿraj (lame), among defects; shahila, giving ashhal (having bluish-grey eyes), among beauties; khaḍira al-zarʿ, giving akhḍar (green), among colours; and lamiya, giving almā (having dark lips), among adornments. For colours, defects and visible beauties have been treated like fixed physical features that neither increase nor decrease — like the hand, the foot and the other limbs — in that one does not express wonder at them.
A ninth condition:
There is a ninth condition which many grammarians have neglected although it is very important, namely that it not be dispensed with by what is formed from another (word); e.g. qāla, from al-qāʾila (the midday nap): they do not say mā aqyalahu, making do with their saying mā akthara qāʾilatahu ("how much he takes the midday nap!") — Sībawayh mentioned it; and e.g. sakira (to be drunk), qaʿada and jalasa (to sit): they do not say mā askarahu, mā aqʿadahu and mā ajlasahu, making do with their saying mā ashadda sukrahu ("how drunk he is!") and mā akthara quʿūdahu wa-julūsahu ("how much he sits!"). Ibn ʿUṣfūr added qāma, ghaḍiba and nāma; but Sībawayh reported mā anwamahu, and they said "more sleepy than a lynx (fahd)".
How to arrive at wonder from what lacks some of the conditions:
One arrives at wonder from what has more than three letters, and from what is described on the pattern afʿal faʿlāʾ, by means of mā ashadda and the like, putting their maṣdar in the accusative after it, and by means of ashdid and the like, putting their maṣdar in the genitive after it. So you say: mā ashadda inṭilāqahu or ḥumratahu ("how fast his setting off is / how intense his redness is!"), and ashdid bi-inṭilāqihi wa-ḥumratihi. For the negated and the passive, their maṣdar is interpreted, not explicit, e.g. mā akthara an lā yaqūma ("how often he does not stand!") and mā ashadda mā ḍuriba ("how hard he was beaten!"), and ashdid bihimā [i.e. with them in the ashdid bi- form]. As for the incomplete verb, its maṣdar is brought, if it has a maṣdar, in the manner described, e.g. mā ashadda ṣayrūratahu jamīlan ("how thoroughly he has become handsome!"). As for the non-inflecting verb and what does not admit of degrees, one does not express wonder from them at all.
3- On aḥad, and the difference between al-aḥad and al-wāḥid:
Aḥad is more complete than wāḥid. Do you not see that when you say "So-and-so — not one (wāḥid) can stand up to him", it is possible in meaning that two or more can stand up to him, unlike your saying "no one (aḥad) can stand up to him"? And aḥad has a particularity that wāḥid does not have: you say "there is no one (aḥad) in the house", and it may include animals, birds, wild beasts and humans, so it covers people and others, unlike "there is not one (wāḥid) in the house", which is specific to human beings.
Aḥad comes in the speech of the Arabs in the sense of wāḥid, and is then used in negation and affirmation, e.g. «قل هو الله أحد», i.e. one; and the first [Translator's note: printed «وأول», sense unclear], «فابعثوا أحدكم بورقكم». Otherwise it is only used in negation: you say "no one (min aḥad) came to me", and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد». Wāḥid is used in both without restriction. Aḥad is used for masculine and feminine; Allah the Exalted said «لستنّ كأحد من النساء», unlike wāḥid: one does not say "like a wāḥid of the women" but "like a wāḥida". Aḥad is suitable for singular and plural, and for this reason it is described (by a plural) in His saying «من أحد عنه حاجزين», unlike wāḥid. Al-aḥad has a plural from its own root, namely al-aḥadūn and al-āḥād, whereas wāḥid has no plural from its own root: one does not say wāḥidūn, but rather two, three. And al-aḥad is excluded from entering into any reckoning, unlike al-wāḥid. From this, seven differences emerge.
4- The story of the interruption of revelation for a limited period:
The story of the interruption of revelation must be detailed here. The narrators have mentioned that Quraysh resorted to a terrible means to combat the influence of the Qur'an: they sent a delegation [Translator's note: printed «فدا» for «وفدا»] to the Jews of Yathrib to ask them about the means by which they could resist this thing that Muhammad had brought. The Jews asked them to question the Prophet about certain matters. When they returned to Mecca, they went to him and said: "O Muhammad, tell us about youths who went away in the first age and had a wondrous story, and about a man who travelled widely and reached the east and west of the earth; and tell us about the spirit — what is it?" The Prophet said to them:
- I will tell you tomorrow about what you have asked.
The Messenger of Allah was waiting for revelation to come down to him containing the answer to what Quraysh had asked about; but the revelation was delayed for the Prophet for fifteen days, and Quraysh were overjoyed at his inability to answer, and said: "Muhammad promised us tomorrow, and today it is fifteen nights in which we have been waiting, and he has not told us anything of what we asked him." The interruption of revelation grieved the Prophet greatly, and what the people of Mecca were saying added to his anxiety. At the end of that day Gabriel came down, and he greeted him at once by saying:
- You have kept away from me, O Gabriel, until I came to think ill. Gabriel replied to him with the noble verse: «وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك، له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا». Then Gabriel began to teach the Prophet Sūrat al-Kahf, in which — as will come — there is an answer to what Quraysh asked and a splendid detailing of many matters that occupied minds at that time. The answers of Sūrat al-Kahf cut off their way, and they could not return any reply or answer.

dervis-irab:29-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَعْتَدْنا): meaning "we prepared and made ready". In al-Qāmūs: "ʿattada and aʿtada al-shayʾ: he made it ready and prepared it; ʿatida al-shayʾ yaʿtadu (of the pattern ẓarufa and jamila) ʿatādan: it became ready; taʿattada in his craft: he was meticulous in it. Al-ʿatād is what is prepared for some purpose, and everything made ready of weapons and implements of war; the plural is aʿtud, ʿutud and aʿtida."
(سُرادِقُها): al-surādiq, with a ḍamma on the sīn and a kasra on the dāl, is the large tent stretched over the courtyard of a house; also the tent, and the dust or smoke that rises and surrounds a thing; the plural is surādiqāt. In al-Kashshāf: "He likened the fire that surrounds them to the surādiq, which is the enclosure around a tent; a bayt musaradaq is one that has a surādiq. It is also said that it is smoke that surrounds the disbelievers before they enter the Fire, and it is said that it is a wall of fire encircling them." Al-Rāghib said: "Al-surādiq is Persian, arabicized, and in their speech there is no other singular noun whose third letter is an alif followed by two letters except this one." In al-Mukhtār: al-surādiq is singular and the plural is surādiqāt; it is what is stretched over the courtyard of the house, and every house made of kursuf, that is cotton, is a surādiq; one says bayt musaradaq.
Al-Jawharī said: "Al-surādiq is the singular of al-surādiqāt, which are what is stretched over the courtyard of the house, and every house of kursuf is a surādiq." From it is the saying of Ruʾba:
يا حكم بن المنذر بن جارود ... سرادق المجد عليك ممدود
(O Ḥakam ibn al-Mundhir ibn Jārūd, the surādiq of glory is stretched over you.)
And another poet said:
هو المدخل النعمان بيتا سماؤه ... صدور الفيول بعد بيت مسردق
(He is the one who made al-Nuʿmān enter a house whose sky was the chests of elephants, after a house with a surādiq.)
Sallām ibn Jandal said this when the king of the Persians killed the Arab king al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir under the feet of elephants.
(المهل): with a ḍamma on the mīm; a name that gathers the mineral substances such as silver, iron and brass, whatever of them is molten; also thin tar; thin oil; poison; pus, or specifically the pus of a dead person; the ashes that fall off bread; and it is said that it is like the dregs of oil, that is, what remains of it in the vessel. In sum, it is a comprehensive name for every filthy thing that turns the stomach, pains the soul and makes it recoil.
(مُرْتَفَقاً): this root was mentioned earlier in this sūra. Here it means a place to recline, from al-mirfaq (the elbow), and this is for the sake of correspondence (mushākala) with the later phrase "وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً"; otherwise the people of the Fire have no reclining and no leaning. It may also be of the kind of the verse:
إني أرقت فبت الليل مرتفقا ... كأن عيني فيها الصاب مذبوح
(I was sleepless and spent the night propped on my elbow, as though in my eye were crushed ṣābʾ.)
Irtifāq is leaning on the elbow with the forearm upright, which is the posture of the grieving and the sorrowful. Al-ṣāb is a bitter plant like colocynth, and al-madhbūḥ means split open; it is an allusion to weeping and the pouring of tears. The verse is by Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī.
(السندس): the thin kind of brocade (dībāj).
(الاستبرق): the thick kind of brocade. Istabraq is Greek, and sundus is Persian; it is also said Indian. Both were mentioned earlier in a table in which we counted the foreign (non-Arabic) words.

* I'rab:
(وَقُلِ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ وَمَنْ شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ) «الحق» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من ربكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also permissible that «الحق» be a mubtadaʾ and «من ربكم» its khabar. «فمن شاء»: the فاء is resumptive; «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; «شاء» is a past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa" (he). The فاء in «فليؤمن» is the connecting particle of the apodosis, because the clause is of the requestive kind; the لام is the lām of command; «يؤمن» is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām of command. «ومن شاء فليكفر» is conjoined to the preceding one.
(إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنا لِلظَّالِمِينَ ناراً أَحاطَ بِهِمْ سُرادِقُها) «إن» and its noun; the clause «أعتدنا» is its predicate; «للظالمين» is attached to «أعتدنا»; «نارا» is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); the clause «أحاط بهم سرادقها» is an adjective (naʿt) of «نارا»; «أحاط» is a past verb, «بهم» is attached to «أحاط», and «سرادقها» is the agent (fāʿil) of «أحاط».
(وَإِنْ يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغاثُوا بِماءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ) The واو is a conjunction, and «إن» is conditional; «يستغيثوا» is the protasis, jussive, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the واو is the agent; «يغاثوا» is the apodosis; «بماء» is attached to «يغاثوا»; «كالمهل» is an adjective of «ماء»; the clause «يشوي الوجوه» is a second adjective or a ḥāl, and «الوجوه» is a direct object. [Translator's note: the source prints «الوجود» in the explanation, which is evidently a misprint for «الوجوه».]
(بِئْسَ الشَّرابُ وَساءَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً) «بئس» is a rigid past verb, one of the verbs of blame; «الشراب» is its agent; the specified object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, that is, "it" (hiya). «ساءت» is conjoined to «بئس», and «مرتفقا» is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the agent, that is, "its place of reclining" (murtafaquhā). Pay no attention to whoever parsed it as a maṣdar (verbal noun). [Translator's note: the source prints «مرتفا» in the explanation, evidently a misprint for «مرتفقا».]
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ إِنَّا لا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا) «إن» and its noun; the clause «آمنوا» is a ṣila (relative clause); «وعملوا الصالحات» is conjoined to «آمنوا». As for «إنا لا نضيع», it is permissible that this clause be the predicate of «إن», or you may make it parenthetical. «إن» and its noun, and the clause «لا نضيع» is its predicate; the agent of «نضيع» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu" (we); «أجر» is a direct object; «من» is a relative noun, a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «أحسن» is a ṣila; «عملا» is a tamyīz, and it is also permissible that it be a direct object. The agent of «أحسن» is the pronoun "huwa". This is the connector (rābiṭ) if you make «إنا لا نضيع» the predicate of «إن الذين»; otherwise the connector is the repetition of the overt noun in its meaning.
(أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهارُ) The clause is a second predicate of «إن الذين», or the predicate if you make the clause «إنا لا نضيع» parenthetical. «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ; «لهم» is a fronted predicate; «جنات عدن» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the second mubtadaʾ with its predicate is the predicate of «أولئك». The clause «تجري من تحتهم الأنهار» is a ḥāl from «جنات» or an adjective of it. Thus they have by this two kinds of reward out of five kinds, and the remaining three are:
(يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِياباً خُضْراً مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ) «يحلون» is an imperfect passive verb, and the واو is the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); «فيها» is a ḥāl, that is, "while they are in Paradise", or is attached to «يحلون»; «من أساور» is attached to an omitted element, an adjective of an omitted object, that is, "ornaments (ḥulīyan) of gold"; «من ذهب» is an adjective of «أساور». «يلبسون» is conjoined to «يحلون», and the واو is the agent; «ثيابا» is a direct object; «خضرا» is an adjective; «من سندس» is an adjective or a ḥāl from «ثيابا»; «إستبرق» is conjoined to «سندس»; «متكئين» is a ḥāl from «أولئك»; «فيها» is also a ḥāl, so they are nested (mutadākhila); «على الأرائك» is attached to «متكئين». Thus the five ample blessings are completed.
(نِعْمَ الثَّوابُ وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً) The parsing of its counterpart has already been given, so refresh your acquaintance with it.

* Rhetoric:
These verses contain many rhetorical arts, most of which have been mentioned before, so we will content ourselves with pointing to them.

1- Mockery (al-tahakkum):
In His saying, the Exalted, «يغاثوا بماء كالمهل», He called the highest kind of punishment "relief" (ighātha), though ighātha is rescue from punishment, by way of mocking them and taking satisfaction against them. Tahakkum is a charming art of theirs, derived from tahakkamat al-biʾr (the well collapsed), or from tahakkum in the sense of intense anger or regret over something that has passed. In it the glad tidings are a warning, the promise is a threat, and the honouring of the one addressed, who is being mocked, is contempt. This verse is among the best examples of it, since He made relief the opposite of relief itself; so beside the mockery there is also correspondence (mushākala). The poets were enamoured of this meaning; one of them took it word for word, and did well in one respect but erred in the construction, saying as he satirized a miser:
أبات الضيوف على سطحه ... فبات يريهم نجوم السماء
وقد فتت الجوع أكبادهم ... وان يستغيثوا يغاثوا بماء
(He made the guests spend the night on his roof, and he spent the night showing them the stars of the sky; hunger had crushed their livers, and if they cry for help they are helped with water.)
Among our poets Ibn al-Rūmī excelled in it, and we cited examples of his mockery; we now cite verses of his in which he mocks the owner of a long beard:
ارع فيها الموسى فإنك منها ... يشهد الله في اثام كبير
أيما كوسج يراها فيلقى ... ربه بعدها صحيح الضمير
هو أحرى بأن يشك ويغرى ... باتهام الحكم في التقدير
لحية أهملت فسالت وفاضت ... فإليها تشير كف المشير
ما رأتها عين امرئ ما رآها ... قط إلا أهلّ بالتكبير
روعة تستخفه لم يرعها ... من رأى وجه منكر ونكير
فاتق الله ذا الجلال وغيّر ... منكرا فيك ممكن التغيير
أو فقصّر منها فحسبك منها ... نصف شبر علامة التذكير
(Pasture the razor upon it, for with regard to it you are, Allah is witness, in great sin. Any beardless man who sees it will meet his Lord afterwards with a sound conscience; he is more likely to doubt and be incited to accuse the Judge in His decree. A beard left untended, which flowed and overflowed, to which the hand of the pointer points. No eye of any man has seen it, none has ever seen it, but he cried "Allahu akbar". A awe that unsettles him, which the one who sees the faces of Munkar and Nakīr is not struck by. So fear Allah, the Possessor of Majesty, and change a wrong in you that can be changed; or else shorten it, for enough for you of it is half a span, the mark of masculinity.) [Translator's note: the Arabic text of these verses is printed with some corruption in the source; the gloss follows the sense as best it can be read.] And his sophistry is evident, arising from the inner sense of the beard's awesomeness, so that even al-Buḥturī's beard was not safe from his satire, when he says:
البحتري ذنوب الوجه تعرفه ... وما رأينا ذنوب الوجه ذا أدب
(Al-Buḥturī: you know the "tail of the face"; and we have never seen one with a "tail of the face" possessing refinement.)

2- Emphatic simile (al-tashbīh al-muʾakkad):
In His saying, the Exalted, «إنا اعتدنا للظالمين نارا أحاط بهم سرادقها», He likened the fire that surrounds them to the surādiq pitched over those it encloses, and the surādiq was annexed to the fire. That is the emphatic simile, which is when the likened (mushabbah) is annexed to the thing likened to (mushabbah bihi), as in the saying of one of them:
والريح تعبث بالغصون وقد جرى ... ذهب الأصيل على لجين الماء
(The wind plays with the branches, and the gold of the evening has flowed over the silver of the water.)
He annexed al-aṣīl (the evening), which is the likened, to al-dhahab (gold), which is the thing likened to, as he annexed al-māʾ (water), the likened, to al-lujayn (silver), the thing likened to. Shawqī eyed it and said describing Damascus:
دخلتها وحواشيها زمردة ... والشمس فوق لجين الماء عقيان
(I entered it, and its outskirts were emerald, and the sun above the silver of the water was pure gold.)
What is meant by the emphatic simile is his phrase "لجين الماء"; as for "حواشيها زمردة" and "الشمس عقيان", they belong to the eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-baligh) in which the particle is concealed.

3- Correspondence (al-mushākala):
That is in His saying «وساءت مرتفقا». He mentioned irtifāq for correspondence with His later saying in describing the people of Paradise «وحسنت مرتفقا», because reclining of the hand in the Fire is not valid; rather in it are torment and harm. We mentioned in the Vocabulary section that irtifāq may arise from worry and torment, as in the verse of al-Hudhalī cited above, in which case there is no mushākala. Among the charming examples of mushākala is the saying of one of them, whom his brothers invited to a morning drink while he had no clothes to wear, so he wrote to them:
إخواننا قصدوا الصبوح بسحرة ... وأتى رسولهم إليّ خصيصا
قالوا التمس شيئا نجد لك طبخة ... قلت اطبخوا لي جبة وقميصا
(Our brothers aimed at the morning drink at dawn, and their messenger came to me specially. They said, "Seek something and we will find you a dish." I said, "Cook me a jubba and a shirt.")
It is useful to point out the feminine form of «حسنت» and «ساءت», which is according to the meaning, that is, "the Fire was evil as a place of reclining and the Garden was good as a place of reclining".

4- Istitbāʿ (the entailing addition):
This is a beautiful art that thoroughly covers the thing one sets out to write about, by exhaustively listing the attributes that surround it and suit it, so that the speaker hardly mentions one meaning or takes up one purpose before entailing another meaning of its kind that calls for adding to its description. Thus He, the Exalted, mentioned Paradise as the reward of those who believed and did righteous deeds, and described it as having rivers flowing through it beneath them; then He mentioned bracelets as an ornament for them, in indefinite form to leave their beauty beyond description; and He joined sundus and istabraq, the thin and the thick of silk garments, after the custom of the pampered, who prepare clothes for summer that suit it and other garments for winter that suit the states of severe cold. He singled out reclining for mention because it is the posture of the pampered and luxuriating, relaxed on seats and couches in delightful halls and lofty palaces. Glory be to the One who spoke these words.
An example of istitbāʿ in poetry is the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
نهبت من الأعمار ما لو حويته ... لهنئت الدنيا بأنك خالد
(You have plundered of lifespans what, had you possessed it, the world would have been congratulated that you are immortal.)
He made his praise of him for courage entail praise of him as a cause of the world's well-being, since he made the world congratulated on his immortality, because he is the cause of its flourishing. Like it is his saying also:
إلى كم ترد الرسل عما أتوا به ... كأنهم فيما وهبت ملام
(How long will you turn back the envoys from what they came with, as though they, in what you have given, were blame?)
He praised Sayf al-Dawla for courage here too, and in the rest of the verse made his praise for generosity follow, through his disobeying of blame about gifts. The meaning is that you turn them away from what they ask of the truce as you turn away the blame of those who blame you for giving; that is, just as you do not listen to the reproach of a reproacher about your generosity, so you do not accept the truce. This is among the most marvellous things minds devise. It is useful to cite selected verses from this poem, which he composed in praise of Sayf al-Dawla when the envoys of the Byzantines came to him asking for a truce in the year 344, and which begins:
أراع كذا؟ كل الملوك همام ... وسح له رسل الملوك غمام؟
(Is it thus that he terrifies? Every king is a hero, and the envoys of kings pour down upon him like clouds?)
He says: has any king terrified all kings as I see you terrify them, and have envoys streamed to any king as they have streamed to you? He made the succession of envoys to him like the pouring of clouds. In the verse there is barāʿat al-istihlāl (excellence of opening), because in it, being the opening of the poem, he alluded to the subject of the envoys. Then he said:
ودانت له الدنيا فأصبح جالسا ... وأيامها فيما يريد قيام
(The world submitted to him, so he sat, while its days stood at his service in whatever he wants.)
إذا زار سيف الدولة الروم غازيا ... كفاها لمام لو كفاه لمام
(If Sayf al-Dawla visits Byzantium as a raider, a mere brief visit would suffice them, if a brief visit sufficed him.)
فتى يتبع الأزمان في الناس خطوه ... لكل زمان في يديه زمام
(A youth whose step follows the ages among the people; for every age there is a rein in his hands.)
تنام لديك الرسل أمنا وغبطة ... وأجفان رب الرسل ليس تنام
(The envoys sleep by you in safety and joy, while the eyelids of the envoys' lord do not sleep.)
حذارا لمعرورى الجياد فجاءة ... إلى الطعن قبلا ما لهن لجام
(For fear of horses ridden bareback, suddenly facing the thrust, which have no bridle.)
تعطف فيه والأعنة شعرها ... وتضرب فيه والسياط كلام
(You turn them in it, their reins being their hair, and you strike in it, the whips being words.)
إلى كم ترد الرسل عما أتوا به ... كأنهم فيما وهبت ملام
(How long will you turn back the envoys from what they came with, as though they, in what you have given, were blame?)
وإن كنت لا تعطي الذمام طواعة ... فعوذ الأعادي بالكريم ذمام
(Even if you do not grant protection willingly, enemies' taking refuge with the generous is itself protection.)
وإن نفوسا أممتك منيعة ... وإن دماء أملتك حرام
(Souls that sought you are inviolable, and blood that hoped in you is sacrosanct.)
And in it he says:
وشر الحمامين الزؤامين عيشة ... يذل الذي يختارها ويضام
(The worst of the two deaths, the swift ones, is a life in which the one who chooses it is humbled and wronged.)
فلو كان صلحا لم يكن بشفاعة ... ولكنه ذل لهم وغرام
(Had it been a peace it would not have come by intercession, but it is humiliation for them and ruin.)

dervis-irab:45-51.t:
* Vocabulary:
(هَشِيماً): dry, with its parts scattered. Al-Zamakhsharī said: al-hashīm is what has been shattered and broken; the singular is hashīma. Ibn Qutayba said: everything that was fresh and then dried up is hashīm. One says "the earth became hashīm", meaning that the plants and trees on it dried up and broke apart. The letter hāʾ together with shīn, as fāʾ and ʿayn of the root, has the special sense of breaking, shattering and softness, and of anything that does not resist. So al-hashsh is what is soft and tender in anything; "a hashsha loaf" is one soft where it is broken; and one says "so-and-so is hashsh al-maksar", meaning easy to deal with in the needs sought from him, which may be said in praise or in blame. Al-hashīsh is like al-hashīm. Hashara al-nāqa: to milk out everything in her udder. A "hashira" or "hashūr" tree is one whose leaves fall quickly. Al-hayshar among men is the soft, weak, tall one. Al-hashm among mountains means the soft ones. Tahashshamat al-arḍ: the land became barren because rain was cut off from it.
(تَذْرُوهُ): scatters it and strews it. One says dharat al-rīḥ al-turāb (the wind scattered the dust); adhrat al-ʿayn damʿahā (the eye shed its tear); ʿaynāhu tudhriyāni al-dumūʿ (his eyes shed tears); "I stabbed him and adhraytuhu off his horse", and adhāhu al-faras ʿan ẓahrihi means the horse threw him off its back. Dharā ḥadda nābihi means his teeth were ground down and their tops fell off. "A dharw of speech from him reached me", meaning a part of it; and "he took up a dharw of the conversation" when he hinted and did not speak plainly. Ṣakhr ibn Ḥabnāʾ said:
أتاني عن مغيرة ذرو قول ... وعن عيسى فقلت له كذاك (A bit of talk reached me about Mughīra, and about ʿĪsā, and I said to him: so be it.)
(نُغادِرْ): we leave. One says ghādara and aghdarahu when he left it. From it comes al-ghadr, the abandonment of fidelity. Al-ghadīr is what the flood has left behind. Al-ghadīra is hair that has grown down until it is long; the plural is ghadāʾir.

* I'rab:
(وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا كَماءٍ أَنْزَلْناهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ): The wāw is resumptive. اضرب is an imperative verb. لهم is attached to اضرب. مثل الحياة الدنيا is the first direct object (mafʿūl bihi), and the kāf is the second direct object. The clause أنزلناه من السماء is an adjective (naʿt) of ماء. It is also possible that اضرب has the meaning of "mention", so that it takes one object, in which case the kāf is the predicate of an omitted subject, or is attached to the sense of the verbal noun (maṣdar), that is, "a likening like water".
(فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَباتُ الْأَرْضِ): The fāʾ is a conjunction. اختلط is a past verb. به is attached to اختلط. نبات الأرض is the agent (fāʿil). The secret of this simile will come in the section on rhetoric. (فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيماً تَذْرُوهُ الرِّياحُ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقْتَدِراً): فأصبح is conjoined to اختلط. The subject of أصبح is a latent pronoun referring to نبات الأرض. هشيما is the predicate of أصبح. The clause تذروه الرياح is an adjective of هشيما. وكان: the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāl). كان and its subject; مقتدرا is its predicate. على كل شيء is attached to مقتدرا. (الْمالُ وَالْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): المال is the mubtadaʾ (subject). البنون is conjoined to المال. زينة الحياة is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and الدنيا is an adjective.
(وَالْباقِياتُ الصَّالِحاتُ خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ ثَواباً وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًا): The wāw is resumptive. الباقيات is the mubtadaʾ and الصالحات an adjective. خير is the khabar (predicate) of الباقيات. The comparative sense is not in its usual meaning, because the adornment of this world contains no good; or else it is in its usual meaning, according to the claim of the ignorant and the deluded. عند ربك is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl. ثوابا is a tamyīz (specification). خير أملا is conjoined to خير ثوابا. (وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الْجِبالَ وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ بارِزَةً):
The adverbial noun is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "mention". The clause نسير is the genitive complement of the adverbial noun, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we". الجبال is the direct object. ترى الأرض is conjoined to what precedes. The agent of ترى is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and الأرض is the direct object. بارزة is a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual. (وَحَشَرْناهُمْ فَلَمْ نُغادِرْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَداً): The wāw here is for ḥāl. حشرناهم is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, meaning: "We bring about the moving of the mountains while they are gathered, so that they see those terrors with their own eyes." Or the wāw is a conjunction and the past is meant for the future, that is, "and We shall gather them". It is useful to cite here what al-Zamakhsharī said on this point: "If you say: why was حشرناهم brought in the past tense after نسير and ترى? I say: to indicate that their gathering is before the moving and before the appearing, so that they may witness those great terrors." Then فلم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive. نغادر is an imperfect verb made jussive by لم, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we". منهم is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of أحدا. أحدا is a direct object. (وَعُرِضُوا عَلى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا): [Translator's note: the source text is damaged here; it prints "بهَ عُرِضُوا عَلى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا", and the verse is read here as وَعُرِضُوا.] The wāw is a conjunction on وحشرناهم, entering within its scope. عرضوا is a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). على ربك is attached to عرضوا. صفا is a ḥāl from the wāw in عرضوا. [Translator's note: the source prints the opening of the verse as "َقَدْ", with the lām lost.] (لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونا كَما خَلَقْناكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ):
The lām is the answer to an omitted oath. قد is a particle of confirmation. جئتمونا is a verb, agent and direct object. كما is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, or a ḥāl. خلقناكم is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position. أول مرة is accusative as an adverbial, attached to خلقناكم. The clause لقد جئتمونا is circumstantial, or is the content of an omitted saying.
[Translator's note: the source prints the opening as "َلْ", with the first letter lost.] (بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِداً)
بل is a particle of rejection of the previous. زعمتم is a verb and agent. أن is the lightened form of the heavy (أنّ), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity. نجعل is an imperfect verb made accusative by لن, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we", and the clause is the khabar of أن. لكم is the second direct object and موعدا the first direct object of نجعل. موعدا may denote time or place. If the "making" is merely bringing into existence, then لكم is attached to it and موعدا is the direct object. (وَوُضِعَ الْكِتابُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ)
The wāw is a conjunction. وضع is a passive past verb and الكتاب is the deputy agent. فترى: the fāʾ is a conjunction and ترى is a nominative imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". المجرمين is the first direct object and مشفقين the second direct object. The seeing here is of knowledge, but you may make it visual, in which case مشفقين is a ḥāl. مما is attached to مشفقين, and فيه is attached to an omitted element, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
(وَيَقُولُونَ يا وَيْلَتَنا مالِ هذَا الْكِتابِ لا يُغادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّا أَحْصاها): ويقولون is a conjunction. يا is a particle of vocative and ويلتنا is the one addressed (munādā): they call upon their destruction which they have brought upon themselves. More explanation of this vocative will come in the section on rhetoric. ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; لهذا is the khabar; الكتاب is a substitute (badal). The clause لا يغادر is circumstantial. صغيرة is a direct object and ولا كبيرة is conjoined to صغيرة. إلا is a particle of restriction, and the clause أحصاها is an adjective of صغيرة. It is also permissible that it be a second object of يغادر, because it has the meaning of "leave", which takes two objects. The interrogative here is meant merely as astonishment at the book for this precise enumeration. (وَوَجَدُوا ما عَمِلُوا حاضِراً وَلا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَداً): The wāw is a conjunction. وجدوا is a verb and agent. ما is a direct object, and the clause عملوا is a ṣila; or ما is a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle and the interpreted maṣdar is the direct object, that is, "they found their deed". حاضرا is a second direct object. ولا يظلم: the wāw is circumstantial, لا is a negative. يظلم ربك أحدا is a verb, agent and direct object, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

(وَإِذْ قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ): The adverbial noun is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "mention", and the clause قلنا is the genitive complement of the adverbial noun. للملائكة is attached to قلنا. اسجدوا is an imperative verb and agent. لآدم is attached to اسجدوا. فسجدوا is a verb and agent. إلا is a particle of exception and إبليس is the excepted (mustathnā). The exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and it was said to be connected (muttaṣil); this has been settled earlier. (كانَ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ): The clause is resumptive, brought to give the reason after the exception of Iblis from those who prostrated, as though it were the answer to an implied question, namely: why did he not prostrate? So it was said: كان. The subject of كان is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to Iblis, and من الجن is its predicate. ففسق is conjoined to كان. عن أمر ربه is attached to فسق. (أَفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُ وَذُرِّيَّتَهُ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِي وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ بِئْسَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ بَدَلًا): The hamza is for a question of rebuke and astonishment. تتخذونه is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object. As for وذريته, the wāw may be a conjunction, with ذريته conjoined to the hāʾ; or it may have the meaning of "with", with ذريته as mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). أولياء is a second direct object. من دوني is attached to an omitted element, an adjective of أولياء, or is attached to تتخذونه. وهم: the wāw is for ḥāl, and هم is a mubtadaʾ. لكم is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of عدو. عدو is their khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl from the object of تتخذونه or from its agent. بئس is a rigid past verb, to express blame, and its agent is a pronoun concealed and explained by an indefinite noun. للظالمين is attached to بدلا, and بدلا is a tamyīz. It is also possible that للظالمين is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl. The specified subject of the blame is omitted, its implied form being "How evil a substitute: Iblis and his offspring." (ما أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ خَلْقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلا خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ): ما is negative. أشهدتهم is a verb, agent and direct object. خلق السموات والأرض is a second direct object. ولا خلق أنفسهم is conjoined to خلق السموات والأرض. (وَما كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ الْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُداً): The wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. كنت is kāna and its subject, and متخذ is its khabar. المضلين is a muḍāf ilayhi. In it the overt noun is put in the place of the pronoun. عضدا is the second direct object of متخذ. The discussion of this simile will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the saying of the Exalted «واضرب لهم مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض», to the end of the verse, there is a reversed comparative simile (tashbīh tamthīlī maqlūb). As for the comparative simile: the life of this world and the ornaments in it, which astonish the heedless who look at them and enjoy their adornment until, when he recovers from his blindness, he finds that what he was amusing himself with and enjoying is falsehood without reality, is likened to the plant with which the water pouring down from the sky has mingled, so that it swelled, became luxuriant and blossomed, and put forth every delightful kind; the eye had hardly enjoyed it and the soul rejoiced at the sight of it when it withered and turned yellow, then dried and wilted, then became dry chaff scattered by the winds, as though it had never been. As for the reversal: the proper wording would have been "and it mingled with the plant of the earth". Its explanation is that, since each of the two things mixed is described with the attribute of its fellow, it was reversed for emphasis on its abundance. In plainer words: since mingling consists of two things entering into one another, it is true of each of them that it is mingled and mingled with; but in the usage and custom of the language the bāʾ enters upon the greater, non-incidental one, so this was counted as a reversal. And since reversal is acceptable when it carries a point, namely that each of the two is mingled and mingled with, which is emphasis on abundance so that it is as though it were the abundant original, the reversal is meant in the sense we mentioned just above. This is one of the delightful and wonderful things, so know it.
2- The implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in his saying «يا ويلتنا»: the calling of the "woe" rests on likening it to a person whose approach is requested, as though it were said: "O our destruction, come forward, for this is your time."
3- The eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh) in «وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا»: He likened the misleaders to the forearm-support (ʿaḍud) by which a person is strengthened, whose origin is the limb that runs from the elbow to the shoulder, and he did not mention the particle of comparison. Some have made it a metaphor, which is an error, because the two pillars of simile are present, namely the thing likened and that to which it is likened.
4- The use of the general in negation and the particular in affirmation: this is in his saying, the Exalted: «ما لهذا الكتاب لا يغادر صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصاها». For the existence of reckoning over the small entails the existence of reckoning over the great, so it ought to be "it leaves out neither great nor small", since if it leaves out no small one, it is all the more fitting that it leave out no great one; whereas if it leaves out no great one, it is possible that it leaves out a small one. For if He does not pardon the small, then by analogy He ought not to pardon the great; and if He does not pardon the great, it is possible that He pardons the small. [Translator's note: the source's reasoning is as printed here; it is terse and its two sentences are not fully parallel.]
5- In his saying, the Exalted, «المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا» there is the art of combination (fann al-jamʿ), which is that the speaker combines two or more things under a single ruling. It is clear in the verse. An example is in the ḥadīth, the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever wakes in the morning secure in his dwelling, healthy in his body, with the food of his day, it is as though the world had been gathered for him with all its sides (bi-ḥadhāfīrihā)." So he combined security, health of the body and the day's food within the possession of the world with all its sides; ḥadhāfīr means sides, and the singular is ḥadhfār. An example in poetry is the saying of Abū al-ʿAtāhiya:
إن الشباب والفراغ والجدة ... مفسدة للمرء أيّ مفسده
(Youth, leisure and wealth are a corruption for a man, and what a corruption.)
and the saying of Ibn Khafāja al-Andalusī:
تعلقته ريان من خمر ريقه ... له رشفها دوني ولي دونه السكر
وطبنا معا ثغرا وشعرا كأنما ... له منطقي ثغر له ولي ثغره شعر
(I became attached to him, sated with the wine of his saliva; the sipping of it is his without me, and the intoxication is mine without him. We were both delighted together, in mouth and in poetry, as though my speech were a mouth for him, and his mouth were poetry for me.)

dervis-irab:52-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَوْبِقاً): a noun of place or a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun with initial mīm) from wabiqa yabiqu wabūqan, like wathaba yathibu wathūban, or from wabiqa yūbaqu wabaqan, like fariḥa yafraḥu faraḥan, when one perishes; that is, a place of destruction in which they share, and it is the Fire. In al-Qāmūs and elsewhere: wabaqa yabiqu (of the pattern daraba yaḍribu), wabiqa yabaqu (of the pattern ʿalima yaʿlamu), and wabiqa yūbaqu wabaqan, wubūqan and mawbiqan, and istawbaqa: he perished, so he is wabiq. Al-mawbiq is the place of destruction, the appointed time, the prison, and anything that comes between two things. On the authority of al-Ḥasan: mawbiqan means enmity, the sense being an enmity so severe that it is destruction. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-bayn means union, that is, "We made their mutual union in this world a destruction on the Day of Resurrection."
(مَصْرِفاً): a noun of place or of time. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: it means "turning away", so it is a mīmī maṣdar. In al-Kashshāf: maṣrafan means a place of turning aside. He (the poet) said:
أزهير هل عن شيبة من مصرف (O Zuhayr, is there any turning away from old age?)
(جَدَلًا): disputation in falsehood. Al-Farazdaq said:
ما أنت بالحكم الترضي حكومته ... ولا الأصيل ولا ذي الرأي والجدل
(You are not the judge whose judgement is accepted, nor the man of lineage, nor the man of opinion and disputation.)
(قُبُلًا): in plain sight and face to face. In al-Qāmūs: "I saw him qubulan, qubulan, qibalan, qibalan, qabalan, qabīlan and qubaliyyan," meaning in plain sight and face to face. Al-Farrāʾ said: qubulan is the plural of qabīl, meaning scattered, following one another. It was also said: in plain sight; and it was said: suddenly.
(لِيُدْحِضُوا): to nullify and remove, from idḥāḍ al-qadam, which is making the foot slip and removing it from its place. In al-Mukhtār: daḥaḍat ḥujjatuhu: his argument became void (of the pattern khaḍaʿa), and Allah adḥaḍahā; daḥaḍat rijluhu: his foot slipped (of the pattern qaṭaʿa); and al-idḥāḍ is making slip.
(مَوْئِلًا): a refuge and place of shelter. The original sense is "the place of return", from waʾala yaʾilu waʾlan and wuʾūlan, when one takes refuge with it; here it is a mīmī maṣdar. In al-Miṣbāḥ: waʾala ilā Allāh yaʾilu (of the pattern waʿada): he took refuge; the active participle gave the name, and from it come Wāʾil ibn Ḥujr, who was a Companion, and Saḥbān ibn Wāʾil. Waʾala also means he returned; and "to Allah is the mawʾil", that is, the place of return.

* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ نادُوا شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ): The adverbial noun is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "mention", and the clause يقول is the genitive complement of the adverbial noun. نادوا is an imperative verb and agent. شركائي is the direct object. الذين is an adjective (naʿt), and the clause زعمتم is the ṣila (relative clause). The returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "you claimed them to be partners", just as the second object of زعمتم is also omitted. (فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُمْ وَجَعَلْنا بَيْنَهُمْ مَوْبِقاً): Either the clause is conjoined to an implied omitted one, that is, "so they hastened to their gods and called them"; or the past is taken as meaning the future. دعوهم is a verb, agent and direct object. فلم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive, and يستجيبوا is an imperfect verb made jussive by لم, and the wāw is the agent. لهم is attached to يستجيبوا. جعلنا is a verb and agent. بينهم is an adverbial noun attached to an omitted element which is the second object, and موبقا is the first object. The meaning is: "We made between the idols and their worshippers a place in which they gather so as to perish together." (وَرَأَى الْمُجْرِمُونَ النَّارَ فَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ مُواقِعُوها): ورأى المجرمون النار is a verb, agent and direct object. فظنوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ظنوا is a verb and agent; إن with its noun and khabar stand in the place of the two objects of ظنوا. The meaning is: it appeared to them from a distant place, and they were certain that they were to fall into it. Thinking (ẓann) here has the meaning of certainty, because that time is not a time of doubt.
(وَلَمْ يَجِدُوا عَنْها مَصْرِفاً): The wāw is a conjunction. ولم يجدوا is conjoined to ظنوا. عنها is attached to مصرفا, because it is a derived noun of place or time, or a mīmī maṣdar with the sense of "turning away". مصرفا is a direct object. (وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ لِلنَّاسِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ): The wāw is a conjunction, and the lām is the answer to an omitted oath. قد is a particle of confirmation. صرفنا is a verb and agent. في هذا is attached to صرفنا, and القرآن is a substitute for هذا. للناس is also attached to صرفنا. من كل is an adjective of an omitted described noun, which is the object of صرفنا, that is, "a strange and wondrous meaning that resembles a proverb in its strangeness and novelty". مثل is a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَكانَ الْإِنْسانُ أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلًا): The wāw is a conjunction or for ḥāl. كان الإنسان: kāna and its subject; أكثر شيء is its khabar; جدلا is a tamyīz. It means that man is, of all living creatures, the most given to disputation and futile obstinacy. (وَما مَنَعَ النَّاسَ أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا إِذْ جاءَهُمُ الْهُدى): The wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. منع is a past verb, and الناس is a direct object put first. أن يؤمنوا is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the second object of منع. إذ is an adverbial noun for time past, attached to يؤمنوا, and the clause جاءهم الهدى is the genitive complement of the adverbial noun. (وَيَسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ الْأَوَّلِينَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ الْعَذابُ قُبُلًا): ويستغفروا is conjoined to يؤمنوا, and the wāw is the agent. ربهم is a direct object. إلا is a particle of restriction [Translator's note: the source prints "حضر", presumably a slip for "حصر"]. أن and what is within its scope is the agent of منع. تأتيهم is an imperfect verb with a direct object put first; سنة الأولين is a delayed agent. أو is a conjunction, and يأتيهم العذاب is conjoined to تأتيهم سنة الأولين. قبلا is a ḥāl from the pronoun or from العذاب. It is necessary to posit an omitted muḍāf before أن تأتيهم سنة الأولين, its implied form being "waiting for the coming". They said: "The muḍāf needed to be posited only because it is impossible to make the coming of the way of the ancients a preventer of their belief, since the preventer accompanies the thing prevented, while the coming of the punishment is later than their belief by a long time." (وَما نُرْسِلُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. نرسل المرسلين is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object. إلا is a particle of restriction. مبشرين is a ḥāl and منذرين is conjoined to it.
(وَيُجادِلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالْباطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الْحَقَّ): يجادل is an imperfect verb, and الذين is the agent, and كفروا is the ṣila. بالباطل is attached to يجادل. ليدحضوا: the lām is for cause, and يدحضوا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām. به is attached to يدحضوا and الحق is a direct object. (وَاتَّخَذُوا آياتِي وَما أُنْذِرُوا هُزُواً)
The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive. اتخذوا is a verb and agent. آياتي is a direct object. The wāw is a conjunction, and ما is a relative noun conjoined to آياتي, and the clause أنذروا is a ṣila. It is also possible to make ما a maṣdar particle, with the maṣdar conjoined to آياتي. هزوا is a second direct object. (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ ذُكِّرَ بِآياتِ رَبِّهِ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْها وَنَسِيَ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ): The wāw is resumptive. من is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and أظلم is the khabar. ممن is attached to أظلم. The clause ذكر is a ṣila. بآيات ربه is attached to ذكر. فأعرض is conjoined to ذكر and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he". عنها is attached to أعرض. نسي is conjoined to what precedes. ما is a direct object, and the clause قدمت is a ṣila, and يداه is the agent. (إِنَّا جَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي آذانِهِمْ وَقْراً): إن and its noun; the clause جعلنا is its khabar. على قلوبهم is in the position of accusative as the second direct object of جعلنا, and أكنة is the first direct object. أن يفقهوه: the maṣdar is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). في آذانهم وقرا is conjoined to the two complements of جعلنا. (وَإِنْ تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدى فَلَنْ يَهْتَدُوا إِذاً أَبَداً): The wāw is a conjunction and إن is conditional. تدعهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is a direct object. إلى الهدى is attached to تدعهم. فلن: the fāʾ is the linking particle, and لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity. يهتدوا is made accusative by لن, and the wāw is the agent. إذن is a particle of answer and consequence. أبدا is an adverbial noun attached to يهتدوا. (وَرَبُّكَ الْغَفُورُ ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ لَوْ يُؤاخِذُهُمْ بِما كَسَبُوا لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ الْعَذابَ): وربك: the wāw is resumptive, and ربك is a mubtadaʾ, and الغفور is the khabar, and ذو الرحمة is a second khabar. لو is conditional. يؤاخذهم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent and a direct object. بما is attached to يؤاخذهم, and the clause كسبوا is a ṣila. The lām is the linking one, and عجل is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he". لهم is attached to عجل and العذاب is a direct object. (بَلْ لَهُمْ مَوْعِدٌ لَنْ يَجِدُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ مَوْئِلًا): بل is a particle of rejection of the previous. لهم is a predicate put first, and موعد is a delayed mubtadaʾ. لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity, and يجدوا is an imperfect verb made accusative by لن. من دونه is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl. موئلا is a direct object. (وَتِلْكَ الْقُرى أَهْلَكْناهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا): تلك is a mubtadaʾ, or is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with the pronoun), and القرى is a substitute, and the clause أهلكناهم is the khabar; what is meant is the people of the towns. It is also permissible to parse القرى as the khabar, and the clause أهلكناهم either a ḥāl or a second khabar. لما is an adverbial noun meaning "when", attached to أهلكناهم, and the clause ظلموا is the genitive complement of لما. (وَجَعَلْنا لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ مَوْعِداً): جعلنا is a verb and agent. لمهلكهم is a ḥāl or is attached to موعدا, and موعدا is a direct object. مهلكهم is a mīmī maṣdar annexed to the agent if the verb is intransitive, or annexed to the object if it is transitive.

* Rhetoric:
In his saying, the Exalted, «أو يأتيهم العذاب قبلا» there is agreement of word with difference of meaning. We have cited the meanings of qubul in the section on vocabulary. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad compiled a work on this, as did Abū al-ʿAmaythal al-Aʿrābī, who composed a book handed down from him, which is a mere enumeration of the words whose meanings may be multiple, without committing to an order in the arrangement of the words, and without giving a reason or attempting to find any link between the different meanings.
